nodes.characterization_summary: SEM shows compact and orderly nanosheet array of Ru/P-Fe3O4 grown in situ on 3D conductive IF substrate.
nodes.evidence_snippet: Scanning electron microscopy (SEM) and transmission electron microscopy (TEM) analyses of the as-prepared catalysts show that a compact and orderly nanosheet array of Ru / P - Fe3O4 is grown in situ on the 3D conductive IF substrate (Figure 1b,c and Figure S2).

nodes.characterization_summary: TEM confirms nanosheet morphology and uniform distribution of Fe, O, P elements with few Ru throughout Ru/P-Fe3O4@IF.
nodes.evidence_snippet: Scanning electron microscopy (SEM) and transmission electron microscopy (TEM) analyses of the as-prepared catalysts show that a compact and orderly nanosheet array of Ru / P - Fe3O4 is grown in situ on the 3D conductive IF substrate (Figure 1b,c and Figure S2).

nodes.characterization_summary: SAED pattern confirms diffraction rings of Fe3O4 corresponding to (422), (311), (111), (622) and (731) crystal planes.
nodes.evidence_snippet: The selected area electron diffraction (SAED) pattern (Figure 1d) of Ru / P - Fe3O4@IF confirms the apparent diffraction rings of Fe3O4, which correspond to the (422), (311), (111), (622) and (731) crystal planes.

nodes.characterization_summary: HRTEM reveals lattice spacing of 0.489 nm and 0.267 nm corresponding to (111) and (311) crystal planes of Fe3O4; increased interplanar distance of (311) plane due to element doping.
nodes.evidence_snippet: The high-resolution transmission electron microscopy (HRTEM) image of Ru / P - Fe3O4@IF (Figure 1e) distinctly reveals lattice spacing values of 0.489 and 0.267 nm, corresponding to the (111) and (311) crystal planes of Fe3O4, respectively.

properties.description: High-resolution TEM image with lattice fringes and insets

nodes.characterization_summary: ICP shows Ru content of approximately 1.08 wt% confirming Ru doping.
nodes.evidence_snippet: Furthermore, the Ru contents of the Ru / P - Fe3O4@IF are approximately 1.08 wt % demonstrated by inductively coupled plasma (ICP), which proves that Ru exists in the form of doping in Ru / P - Fe3O4@IF (Table S1).

nodes.characterization_summary: XRD shows strong diffraction peaks at 18.3°, 30.1°, 35.4°, 43.1°, 56.9°, 62.5° corresponding to (111), (220), (311), (222), (400), (333), (440) planes of Fe3O4 (PDF# 89-0688); absence of Ru and P peaks confirms doping.
nodes.evidence_snippet: As shown in Figure 2a, strong diffraction peaks of Ru / P - Fe3O4@IF at 18.3, 30.1, 35.4, 43.1, 56.9, and 62.5° appear, corresponding to the (111), (220), (311), (222), (400), (333), and (440) crystal planes of Fe3O4 (PDF# 89-0688).

nodes.characterization_summary: Raman shows peaks at 270, 534, 634 cm⁻¹ attributed to Eg, T2g, Alg vibrational modes of Fe-O bonding in Fe3O4.
nodes.evidence_snippet: The Raman spectrum in Figure 2b further confirms the presence of Fe3O4, exhibiting three dominant peaks at 270, 534, and 634 cm⁻¹ of Ru / P - Fe3O4@IF, which are attributed to the Eg, T2g, and Alg vibrational modes of Fe - O bonding of Fe3O4.

nodes.characterization_summary: XPS confirms presence of Fe, Ru, O, P elements. Fe 2p binding energies at 710.6, 713.4, 723.8, 727.1 eV assigned to Fe²⁺ 2p3/2, Fe³⁺ 2p3/2, Fe²⁺ 2p1/2, Fe³⁺ 2p1/2 with negative shift due to doping. P 2p shows P-O bond at ~133 eV and P 2p3/2, 2p1/2 peaks positively shifted. Ru 3p and O 1s peaks also shifted indicating electron migration.
nodes.evidence_snippet: As exhibited in Figure 2d, the binding energies in the spectra of Fe 2p at 710.6, 713.4, 723.8, and 727.1 eV are assigned to Fe²⁺ 2p3/2, Fe³⁺ 2p3/2, Fe²⁺ 2p1/2, and Fe³⁺ 2p1/2, respectively. The P 2p spectra of both Ru / P - Fe3O4@IF and P - Fe3O4@IF exhibits three major peaks, where peaks at ∼133 eV are related to the P - O bond... The O 1s XPS spectrum (Figure 2g) shows two peaks at 533.3 and 530.9 eV.

nodes.characterization_summary: Water contact angle measurements show Ru/P-Fe3O4@IF demonstrates superhydrophilic nature compared to pristine IF. Underwater gas-bubble contact angle test reveals ultrahydrophobic surface indicating better gas-repellent performance.
nodes.evidence_snippet: Ru / P - Fe3O4@IF demonstrates superhydrophilic nature compared to pristine IF, which is in favor of the rapid diffusion of electrolyte on the Ru / P - Fe3O4@IF surface. Furthermore, Ru / P - Fe3O4@IF also exhibits an ultrahydrophobic surface, which means a better gas-repellent performance.

nodes.characterization_summary: Element mapping demonstrates uniform distribution of Fe, O, and P and few Ru throughout the Ru/P-Fe3O4@IF.
nodes.evidence_snippet: In addition, the typical TEM and the corresponding mapping demonstrate the uniform distribution of Fe, O, and P and few Ru throughout the Ru - Fe3O4@IF (Figure 1g).

nodes.characterization_summary: In situ Raman shows Ru-H peak at 950 cm⁻¹ that gradually intensifies under negative cathode voltage, indicating Ru helps capture more H protons.
nodes.evidence_snippet: Specifically, the in situ Raman spectra of Ru / P - Fe3O4@IF reveal that the peak of Ru - H at 950 cm⁻¹ gradually intensifies as a result of the application of negative cathode voltage.
